canonical_identity.scope: Literal signed Haar kernels on full O(n), Euclidean norm-axis reduction, and two fixed-x Haar L1 conclusions.

verdict: The complete proposed scoped graph is mathematically sound as a source topology. All 21 nodes, all 14 AND-hyperedges, and all 7 exclusions are accepted. This accepts the literal-function theorem slice and its explicit background obligations; it does not certify a Lean implementation or identify the literal function with a Gaussian probability density.

graph_audit.edge_semantics: Every from-array is conjunctive. The two incoming L2 edges are separate alternative derivations; premises within either edge remain jointly required.

node_evidence.evidence: A2.SS2.p2.1 explicitly states n>=3, kappa>=4, Haar distribution on the full O(n), and U:=O11. Full O(n), rather than SO(n), is the source domain.
S3.E4 displays A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I_n-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T). The coefficient 1/4 on the symmetrized matrix is essential to the axis coefficient 1/2.

The source introduces p_O as the density of N(0,A_O^-1), without displaying the full density at A2.SS2.p2.1. The input explicitly declares the standard literal precision formula sqrt(det A_O)/(2*pi)^(n/2)*exp(-v^T A_O v/2) as background. This is a transparent formula choice, not a source claim that a Gaussian law or its normalization has been constructed.

The finite real orthogonal group is closed and bounded in finite matrix space, hence compact, and multiplication/inversion are continuous. Its normalized Haar measure is a Borel probability measure. These are appropriate explicit background facts for the selected matrix topology.

Each entry of A_O is affine in matrix entries. Finite dot products, determinant, real square root, and exponential are continuous. The denominator is the fixed positive real number (2*pi)^((n:Real)/2), so division is continuous. Real square root is continuous even at zero; fixed-x continuity does not need a separate positive-definiteness theorem.

For fixed Euclidean x its coordinate vector is constant in O. The signed literal kernel det(O)*p(O,WithLp.ofLp x) is a continuous real function on compact O(n), thus bounded and Borel measurable. Haar probability then gives finite integral of its absolute value. This proves genuine L1, not merely existence of a default-valued integral.
A2.SS2.SSS2.p4.1 states A_(QOQ^T)=Q A_O Q^T. Expansion of S1 proves it because Q I Q^T=I and (QOQ^T)^T=Q O^T Q^T.

For real orthogonal Q, Q^T Q=Q Q^T=I. Hence det(Q A Q^T)=det(A) and (Qv)^T(Q A Q^T)(Qv)=v^T A v. These are literal matrix identities; neither Gaussian density transport nor probabilistic characterization is needed.
A2.SS2.SSS2.p4.1 explicitly states p_(QOQ^T)(Qx)=p_O(x). With B0, S2 and B3 reproduce this as equality of literal real formulas, keeping sqrt determinant and denominator unchanged.

The same source paragraph explicitly says conjugation preserves Haar measure and determinant sign. For fixed Q, conjugation is a continuous group automorphism, whose pushforward of normalized Haar probability is again normalized Haar probability. Algebraically det(QOQ^T)=det(O).

Writing F(x)=integral det(O)*p(O,x) dHaar, substitute O=C_Q(P)=Q P Q^T. S4 preserves measure and determinant, while S3 makes p(C_Q(P),Qx)=p(P,x). Consequently F(Qx)=F(x). L1 guarantees integrability of both fixed-vector kernels; the coordinate adapter makes the use of Qx well typed in Euclidean coordinates.

The selected EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) uses the l2 inner product. WithLp.ofLp supplies the underlying coordinate function, with inner product equal to the finite coordinate dot product. Conjugating coordinate multiplication v -> Qv by this identification gives an actual Euclidean linear isometry since Q^T Q=I. A plain function-space sup norm could not replace this assertion.

n>=3 ensures Fin n contains j0=0. The Euclidean basis vector e has coordinate delta(j,j0), squared norm 1, and norm 1. For r=norm(x)>=0, WithLp.ofLp(r e) has coordinate r at j0 and zero elsewhere, and norm(r e)=|r|=norm(x), including x=0.

Equal-norm transitivity on Euclidean space is valid with the stated degeneracies. If x=y choose identity, including zero. If x!=y, put u=x-y, so u dot u>0 and equal norms give 2(u dot x)=u dot u. The Householder matrix Q=I-2u u^T/(u dot u) is orthogonal and sends x to y. If either vector has norm zero, both vectors are zero and the identity branch applies. No division by a zero norm or zero difference occurs.

For each fixed x choose y=norm(x)e. B5 proves equal Euclidean norms and B6 supplies a Q_x taking x to y. B4 converts this to the precise coordinate action used in D0. Q_x depends on x but remains fixed during Haar integration over O. No measurable choice of x -> Q_x is required for a pointwise-for-every-x theorem.
A2.Ex58 displays E[det(O)p_O(x)]=E[det(O)p_O(norm(x)e1)]. D0 applied to the Q_x supplied by D1 derives the displayed conclusion for every Euclidean x, including x=0.
A2.SS2.SSS2.p4.m8 states e1^T A_O e1=(kappa+1-(kappa-1)U)/2. Directly from S1, (O+O^T)j0j0=2 O_j0_j0, giving A_j0j0=(kappa+1)/2-(kappa-1)O_j0_j0/2. This matches source indexing 11 via canonical j0=0.
At v=WithLp.ofLp(norm(x)e), all dot-product summands except j0 vanish. Thus v dot (A_O v)=norm(x)^2 A_j0j0=((kappa+1-(kappa-1)O_j0_j0)/2)norm(x)^2. This algebra also holds at zero radius.

B0 has exponent -(v dot A_O v)/2. Substitution of D2 produces exactly -(kappa+1-(kappa-1)O_j0_j0)*norm(x)^2/4. The factor 1/4 is the product of the quadratic-form coefficient 1/2 and the Gaussian exponent coefficient 1/2. The sqrt(det A_O) numerator and real n/2 denominator are untouched.

For fixed x, explicit r(O,x) has a continuous determinant normalization and an exponential of an affine matrix entry times the fixed norm(x)^2. Its signed version is continuous on compact O(n), hence absolutely Haar integrable. Independently, D3 identifies it pointwise with the L1 kernel evaluated at the fixed Euclidean axis vector.

L1 and L2 supply the two required genuine Haar L1 conclusions. S5 gives the original-to-axis signed average equality; D3 rewrites the axis integrand into the explicit O_j0_j0 exponent. The conclusion therefore retains exact source normalization, Euclidean norm, full Haar domain and explicit factor 1/4.

edge_evidence.evidence: These jointly establish the literal signed fixed-vector function, its continuity and a compact probability domain, sufficient for absolute integrability.
Expand the precision matrix and use Q Q^T=I plus the transpose identity. All required algebra is present.
Conjugation preserves the determinant and transformed quadratic form, and B0 gives their precise occurrence in p.
Normalized Haar uniqueness under the continuous inner automorphism proves measure preservation; determinant multiplicativity proves sign preservation.
Measure-preserving substitution, pointwise kernel covariance, genuine fixed-vector L1 and the Euclidean-coordinate identification jointly yield F(Qx)=F(x).
The dimension gives a valid first coordinate and the Euclidean identification supplies the unit basis vector and correct l2 norm.
The Euclidean axis has the same norm as x, transitivity produces a fixed orthogonal map, and B4 transports that map to the literal coordinates.
The fixed-Q parent becomes Ex58 by inserting Q_x. This is the essential bridge beyond merely recording conjugation invariance.
The literal S1 matrix and the valid canonical coordinate evaluate its diagonal with the crucial transpose factor 2.
Coordinates of the scaled basis and dot-product preservation turn the axis quadratic into norm(x)^2 times the computed diagonal.
The exact literal -quadratic/2 exponent changes the axis quadratic denominator 2 into exponent denominator 4.

Direct continuity of the displayed explicit r uses only a fixed coordinate entry, fixed radius and the same continuous normalization; compact probability yields L1. It does not rely on spatial domination.
Apply the for-every-fixed-Euclidean-vector L1 statement at norm(x)e and transfer integrability by D3's pointwise equality.
Both integrability conclusions, Ex58 and the exact pointwise axis rewrite jointly deliver the final explicit signed Haar identity.

exclusion_evidence.evidence: A2.SS2.p2.1 uses a Gaussian density in prose, but the audited B0 explicitly declares only its literal standard formula. The scoped conclusion has no law, normalization or covariance claim; establishing these would require separate probability theory.

exclusion_evidence.claim: Spatial integrability, uniform spatial majorant, Fubini/Tonelli and interchanged integration
exclusion_evidence.evidence: Compactness controls integration over O only after x is fixed. The topology contains no claim that the resulting bound is integrable in x, nor any use of a product-space integral.

exclusion_evidence.evidence: The raw source begins domination after p4.m8 at p4.m9 and Ex59; p4.3 then invokes Fubini and Gaussian integration to obtain Ex60. They are later steps and unnecessary for the fixed-x literal slice.

exclusion_evidence.evidence: These source results concern subsequent averaging or H(lambda), whereas fixed-Q conjugation, Euclidean transitivity and literal matrix algebra already close Ex58 and the axis evaluation.
